name: Tanot–Munabao Highway
history: National Highway 70 runs through the western desert of Rajasthan, roughly parallel to the India–Pakistan border, from Tanot in Jaisalmer district south to Munabao in Barmer district. On the way it passes Longewala, Myajlar and Sundra. It is a thinly trafficked road across open sand country, and its main users are the villages strung along it and the security forces who patrol the frontier.
facts: Runs about 310 km through the far western desert of Jaisalmer and Barmer districts.
Its northern end is at Tanot, known for the Tanot Mata temple, where it meets NH 68.
Its southern end is near Munabao, a border village with a railway station, where it meets NH 25.
Passes Longewala, where a small group of Indian soldiers held off a Pakistani tank attack in the 1971 war.
NH 11, coming from Jaisalmer, begins at this road near Myajlar.
One of the emptiest national highways in the country — long stretches have no settlement at all.
It serves border villages that have very few other road links.
significance: It is a frontier road in the Thar desert, joining border villages and posts from Tanot to Munabao. Roads like this exist as much for security and for the isolated villages along them as for through traffic.

relatedRoads.label: Begins at this road near Myajlar

travelNotes: Remote. Fuel, water and mobile coverage are all unreliable. Some areas near the border need permits, so check locally before travelling.
futureUpgrades: In March 2025 the Union road ministry approved ₹1,237.71 crore to strengthen and widen about 135 km of NH 70 and NH 11 to two lanes, including a stretch of this road through Sundra and Myajlar and the Myajlar–Jaisalmer section of NH 11.
